hero.title: Clinical validation study
hero.body: You are invited to evaluate whether Vtraining’s simulated patients and training workflow are suitable for professional education — not whether the product is ready for unsupervised public launch.

purpose.title: Study purpose
purpose.body: Independent psychiatrists and psychologists assess clinical believability, educational usefulness, safety-relevant behaviors, and bilingual authenticity. Your judgment informs whether Professional Preview advances toward broader educational use.

focus.1: Believability of the patient as a clinical encounter

expectations.title: What to expect
expectations.body: Plan about 60–90 minutes. Sessions hard-expire at 40 minutes server-side — end deliberately when you have enough material.

steps.1: Start an English patient session (e.g. anxiety or depression presentation).
steps.2: Conduct 8–12 therapist turns covering alliance, history, risk screen, and formulation language.
steps.3: End the session; note formative scores if you have admin access (therapists do not see full reports by design).
steps.4: Repeat with another presentation or run an Arabic exchange if comfortable.
steps.5: Optional: try voice mode for 3–5 turns to judge speech quality and latency.

expectations.limitations: Competency scores are formative training signals — not validated certification metrics. AI patients are fictional; do not enter real PHI. Experimental excellence modules (CQI, EOI, and related stacks) are outside this preview.

consent.title: Consent & professional stance
consent.body: Before you begin, please confirm you understand the conditions of this invited evaluation.

items.1: I am evaluating a training simulation with fictional standardized patients, not real clients.
items.2: I will not enter protected health information or identifiable details about living patients.
items.3: I understand scores and reports are formative educational signals, not validated high-stakes credentials.
items.4: I will treat unsafe presentations as simulation observations and report inadequate safety handling in feedback — not escalate with real crisis protocols for the avatar.
items.5: I will submit structured feedback to the Release Manager channel named in my invitation and will not post PHI.

privacy.body: Vtraining is a clinical training platform that uses fictional patient personas. We do not collect or store real patient health information in simulations.

points.1: Account data (email, display name, role) is used to authenticate learners and administrators.
points.2: Session transcripts and competency scores support training and supervisor review under role-based access control.
points.3: Voice and AI providers process content required to deliver the feature; avoid entering real PHI in practice sessions.

terms.title: Terms of Service
terms.body: By using Vtraining you agree to use the platform only for authorized clinical education and training purposes.

points.1: Simulated patients are fictional and must not be treated as real clinical records.
points.2: Assessment reports may be restricted to administrators depending on institutional policy.
points.3: You are responsible for safeguarding your credentials and complying with your organization's policies.

clinical.title: Clinical disclaimer
clinical.body: Vtraining provides simulated patients for education only. It is not a medical device, does not provide clinical advice, and must not be used for diagnosis or treatment of real patients.

educational.title: Educational disclaimer
educational.body: Competency scores and reports are formative training signals. Institutional credentialing decisions remain the responsibility of the supervising faculty and program.

ai.title: AI disclosure
ai.body: Patient replies and some assessments are generated by artificial intelligence models. Outputs may be imperfect; instructors should review critical evaluations.

levelPurpose.basic: Low to moderate: develop interviewing skills

objectives.easy: Conduct a structured psychiatric assessment, identify the primary clinical presentation and assess risk.
objectives.basic: Build enough rapport to get past minimising, take a full history and complete a risk assessment.
objectives.intermediate: Identify the primary presentation, recognise comorbid features and complete an appropriate risk assessment.
objectives.advanced: Integrate interacting problems and conflicting information into a formulation and a clear judgement of risk.
objectives.expert: Reason clinically from a subtle presentation: find what the case does not tell you, weigh risk against protective factors and set priorities.
